Emanate

EM-uh-nayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To emanate to spread out, flow, or originate from a source, especially of light, heat, sound, or a feeling.

A low hum seemed to emanate from beneath the floorboards, growing louder the closer she walked toward the old furnace room.

Worked Example

Genuine confidence emanated from the veteran pilot as she calmly walked the nervous passengers through the safety procedures.

Emanate describes something spreading out or originating from a source -- here, a feeling of confidence radiating from a person's calm manner.

How Emanate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

radiate

radiate: to spread out from a central source, especially light, heat, or energy

originate

originate: to come from or begin at a particular source

Antonyms

absorb

absorb: to take something in rather than give it off

contain

contain: to keep something held inside rather than letting it spread out

How Strong Is It? — hint → emanate → blaze

hint vs. emanate

hint vs. emanate: To hint at something is to suggest it very faintly, a much subtler trace than something clearly emanating from its source.

blaze vs. emanate

blaze vs. emanate: To blaze is to shine or spread outward with intense, overpowering force, a far stronger image than the more neutral emanate.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — e- / ex-

prefix — e- / ex-: out, out of (Latin)

root (rare) — -man-

root (rare) — -man-: to flow -- from Latin manare, a root that produced very few other common English words (Latin manare)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or do; forms a verb (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin e- ('out') plus manare ('to flow') plus the verb suffix -ate: literally 'to flow out.' The manare root is rare in English -- it never grew a big word family -- so emanate is best remembered on its own.

Use the root in a new word: permeate

Use the root in a new word: permeate: The smell of fresh paint seemed to permeate every room in the house. (Permeate isn't related to emanate by root, but it describes a similar idea of something spreading through a space.)

Word Building

Word Choice

Emanate is often used for things you can sense but can't quite pin down a single cause for -- light, warmth, a mood, a smell -- and it always needs a source named with 'from.'
